title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes build a combinatorial and polyhedral theory of 'figures'. A figure is a finite set of cells that is closed under taking faces, roughly a polyhedral or cellular complex. The notes use three relations: a figure G can be a sous-figure (subcomplex) of F; F' can be a subdivision of F (F' -s-> F, the same underlying space); and X ≪ G means X 'refines' G, i.e. X is a subfigure of some subdivision of G. Page 49 set up compatibility with disjoint unions and introduced C6, the induced subdivision: G' = F'|G = {x ∈ F' : x ≪ G}.

Page 50, first part, completes C7 (gluing of subdivisions). Let F = ∪ F_i be a union of subfigures, and let F'_i be subdivisions of F_i. Suppose they agree on overlaps, F'_i|F_i∩F_j = F'_j|F_i∩F_j. Then there is a unique subdivision F' of F with F'|F_i = F'_i for all i. In modern terms, subdivisions form a sheaf on the poset of subfigures for finite covers.

Corollary: two subdivisions F', F'' of F are equal iff they induce the same subdivision on every elementary subfigure F_x, i.e. on every closed cell. This uses the cover of F by its closed cells.

Proposition: let F be a figure, G a subfigure, F' a refinement of F (a subfigure of a subdivision of F), and G' = {X ∈ F' : X ≪ G}. Then G' is a subfigure of F', G' refines G, and G' is the largest subfigure of F' that refines G. Grothendieck stresses that this is not trivial: each X ∈ G' refines G, but that alone does not give that G' refines G.

Proof: by definition of refinement, choose a subdivision F̄' of F with F' ⊂ F̄'. By C6, take the induced subdivision Ḡ' = {X ∈ F̄' : X ≪ G} of G. Then G' = F' ∩ Ḡ'. This is an intersection of two subfigures of F̄', hence a subfigure of Ḡ', hence a refinement of G. Maximality is immediate: any subfigure of F' refining G has all its cells ≪ G.

The next page deduces that G' is the infimum of F' and G for the refinement preorder, with a laborious proof ('ouf ! … coton').

Purpose: to set up a self-contained, foundational calculus of subdivisions and refinements, a lattice-like and sheaf-like structure. It serves Grothendieck's program of a 'tame' or combinatorial analysis situs.
errors: The statement ends 'la plus grande sous-figure de F' qui raffine G'' (as transcribed). The intended statement is clearly 'qui raffine G'; G' itself is trivially the largest subfigure refining G'. This is a slip.

In C7 the overlap condition is written only for i≠j. That is harmless, but the gluing implicitly needs the F_i to be subfigures (face-closed) so that induced subdivisions on F_i∩F_j make sense, which is assumed. No genuine gap.
The proposition's proof does not address independence from the choice of F̄'. This is not needed, since G' is defined intrinsically and only the existence of one F̄' is used.

ideas.what: Gluing (sheaf property) of subdivisions over a finite cover of a complex by subcomplexes, with uniqueness
ideas.modern_name: Subdivisions of a polyhedral complex form a sheaf/stack on subcomplexes; extension of compatible subdivisions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman, Hudson, Rourke–Sanderson), folklore

ideas.what: Two subdivisions coincide iff they coincide on each closed cell
For a refinement F' of F and a subcomplex G, the set of cells of F' lying over G is the largest subcomplex of F' refining G; it is the meet of F' and G in the refinement preorder
ideas.modern_name: Induced subdivision / restriction of a refinement; meet in the refinement order

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of 'refinement' (≪) as subfigure of a subdivision, distinguishing refinement of each cell from refinement of the whole
ideas.where_published: Related programmatic remarks on tame topology appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this calculus

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains careful but standard foundational lemmas of PL/polyhedral topology: gluing of subdivisions, locality, and the induced refinement as a meet. Its only interest is documentary, showing how Grothendieck rebuilt PL foundations from scratch in 1986 as part of his tame-topology program. There is no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '{+$(C,G)$+}' is most likely '(C6)', a reference to C6 (subdivisions induites) on page 49, which justifies the induced subdivision Ḡ' of G.
'sous-figure dimensionnaire $F_x$' should probably read 'sous-figure élémentaire $F_x$', consistent with 'G élémentaire' on page 49.
'c'est donc une sous figure' is better read as 'c'est une sous-figure'. The line opens with 'Soient', and '(je dis que)' introduces the claim.
The final clause in the image reads 'qui raffine G'' as written, but is mathematically meant as 'qui raffine G'.
In the left margin the NB reads roughly 'NB si F'≪F subdivision, G' est la subdivision induite (F'|G)'. This notes that the proposition generalizes C6.
